content:
The Malta Memorial is a war memorial that commemorates the more than 2,000 Commonwealth aircrew who lost their lives during the Second World War while serving in the Mediterranean and North African regions and who have no known grave. It is located in Floriana, Malta, at the entrance to the Grand Harbour.

The memorial was unveiled in 1954 and was designed by British architect Sir Hubert Worthington. It consists of a central column topped with a large bronze eagle, symbolizing the courage and sacrifice of the airmen. Surrounding the column are bronze panels inscribed with the names of the airmen who lost their lives.

The Malta Memorial is maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission and is a significant site of remembrance for those who served and died in the air forces during the war. It is a popular destination for visitors and tourists interested in the history of the Second World War and the role that Malta played in the conflict.
